The file is CRLF: "alpha\r\nbeta\r\ngamma\r\n". I need to replace the line containing 'beta' with exactly one line "BETA", preserving CRLF line endings.

Result should be: alpha\r\nBETA\r\ngamma\r\n

Let me use a tool to read the file first (I've read it with od, but let me cat it too as instructed "always read the file before editing"). Then edit.

I have only bash available it seems. Let me do it carefully with a byte-level replacement using sed, which on Linux handles \r as a literal character. Using `sed 's/^beta\r*$/BETA/'` would remove the \r... Actually sed treats \n as line separator; the \r is part of the line content. So line content is "beta\r". Replacing with "BETA" would lose the \r. Better: sed 's/beta\r/BETA\r/' preserves CRLF.

Let me do: sed -i 's/^beta\r\{0,1\}$/BETA\r/' — simpler: use printf/perl. But perl may not be installed; check. Let's just do:

sed 's/^beta.*$/BETA\r/' crlf.txt > tmp && mv tmp crlf.txt

That yields alpha\r\nBETA\r\ngamma\r\n. Good.

But careful: `.*` in sed matches \r too, so the line "beta\r" becomes "BETA\r". Good.
